title: Android Source Sets and Merge Priority Check

questions.prompt: Which approach best applies android source sets and merge priority?
options: Use narrowly scoped source sets and inspect the merged release artifact according to documented priority.
Assume Kotlin classes override by priority
questions.answer: Use narrowly scoped source sets and inspect the merged release artifact according to documented priority.
questions.explanation: The correct approach preserves Gradle’s lazy model, explicit data flow, variant correctness, functional evidence and operability.

questions.prompt: Resources and Kotlin classes use identical override rules during source-set merging.
questions.explanation: Defining a release class with the same fully qualified name in main and release does not override main; both compile and cause a duplicate-class failure.

questions.prompt: What should be inspected to understand final component export and permissions?
questions.answer: The merged manifest for the exact built variant.
questions.explanation: The answer names the model property that makes the build behaviour predictable rather than relying on incidental script order.
